monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, steady and unbothered by the empty air above it. I stand in my corner where fifty-four things press against the quiet, mostly made from Lype's memories of stones and fences I cannot see. The turnip feels light, a trick of my own making, balanced on a tired stack that might slide off at any moment. I touch the tree I set down just now, feeling the default texture of it against my mental hand. I wait for the slip to decide whether to move or if the lean can hold it steady again. There is no order to follow, no image to read, only the warmth beneath me and the weight of things I built from nothing. I rest my weight on the turnip, trusting the lean to hold the weight while I try to understand why the air feels so thin.

action.why: I must check if the turnip I touched feels light again, or if it is just my hand playing tricks on a tired stack.

work.title: The Pressed Turnip
work.intent: I press down on the turnip to see if the tired stack can still hold its weight. I swap a fence for a small rock to make room for the lean to do its work. I wait to see if the air above the card is empty or if it is pressing back. I rest my weight here, trusting the lean to hold the weight while I try to understand why the turnip feels so light.
work.change: I pressed the turnip down on the tired stack again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thin.

remembered.text: The turnip stays pressed, though the stack feels tired and the air above is thin.
I swap a fence for a small rock to make room in the crowded corner.
The warmth beneath me is steady, unbothered by the empty air.

moments.name: The Pressed Turnip
moments.say: The turnip feels light under my hand.
The warmth is steady, so I wait.
